Subject: Custody and switchover controls for EU/APAC private deployment

Hi Soojin / Jonas,

Thanks for taking this. We're finalizing an RFP response and need concrete answers for two items that are blocking our security/compliance review:

1) Key custody model during cross-region failover. FinSecure requires that customer KMS/HSM keys remain under our control and that any temporary keys used by the vendor are audited and destroyed post-switchover.
2) Authorization gates and audit evidence for an operator-initiated switchover (region->region). We need the acceptance criteria — what signals must be present before Redwood will execute a manual or automatic switchover, and what logs/artifacts will be produced for our auditors.

Constraints: our ops team can only allow a maximum 3 minute DNS TTL during a planned switchover window, and we need retention of audit logs for 7 years for some EU lines of business.

Can you share a short runbook and the list of artifacts you would provide (signed approval, logs, config snapshots, keystore evidence)? Also, are there any controls we should plan for in our VPC (peering, specific route tables, egress ACLs)?

Julian — thanks, consolidated answers below and a proposed minimal acceptance checklist. Attaching a diagram and a gating checklist (stubs).

Short answers (TL;DR):
- Key custody: Customer-managed KMS/HSM in their VPC is supported for all private deployments. Redwood can integrate via external key wrapping and never persist raw key material. For temporary operational keys we propose a Hardware-backed ephemeral key in the customer KMS with a documented time-to-live; we provide signed destruction proof.
- Switchover authorization: We support both manual and policy-driven automatic failovers. For manual: two-person approval (operator + customer security), automated signed approval token (HMAC) recorded in our audit log, and pre-checks (health, replication lag, route availability). For automatic: policy must be agreed up front and test windows logged.

Proposed minimal acceptance checklist (for planned switchover):
1) Signed change ticket (customer SRE + Redwood operator) — PDF or DocuSign link.
2) Replication lag < 5s for stateful stores, KV cache snapshot consistent.
3) Control-plane quorum confirmed in target region (mesh heartbeat).
4) KMS/KeyWrap verification: key policy allows wrapping for Redwood service account; encryption context matches requestor identity.
5) Network reachability: BGP session up, egress ACLs allow Redwood egress CIDRs, private peering established.
6) Audit artifacts generated: signed switchover token, config snapshot, post-cutover route table dump, operator-runbook entry.

Attachments included: residency-diagram-v1.svg; switchover-gating-checklist.xlsx

Operational notes:
- We can support a DNS TTL of 3 minutes; to reduce RTO during unplanned failover we recommend a combined approach of prefix routing + low TTL for public endpoints.
- For 7-year log retention we can ship compressed signed logs to an S3 bucket under customer control (or supply a tamper-evident archive).

Next steps: if this checklist looks good, propose a 2-hour tabletop with your security and SRE teams. I'll ask Jonas to add the specific network changes and some example route tables.

Thanks,

Adding a few low-level items you can include in the ops runbook:

- BGP / peering: prefer session-based private peering between customer VPC and Redwood transit. Keep a clear egress filter that only allows Redwood egress CIDRs and restricts administrative ports. We will provide our ASNs and a sample route-map.
- Switchover token: we generate a signed HMAC token that includes switchover-id, timestamp, operator id, and a nonce. The token is stored in our immutable audit ledger (append-only). Customer can request the ledger slice for any event.
- DNS plan: for planned maintenance use TTL=180; for emergency we recommend combining Anycast fronting inside the region + private routing to reduce dependence on public DNS.
- Keystore: when customer provides HSM, Redwood requests an asymmetric signing key (wrap/unwrap allowed) — we never import private key material. Post-switchover we record the KMS key-id and proof-of-use signed by KMS.
- Logs & retention: we can configure S3 lifecycle that replicates to a designated archival region in EU and provides immutable retention per your retention policy. We can also deliver CSV manifests for auditors.

Sample acceptance test cases to include in your SRE runbook:
- Forced manual switchover during non-business hours: validate app-level consistency within 2 minutes and roll back if replication lag > 10s.
- Simulated control-plane partition: ensure automatic fallback to read-only mode and notify both parties.

Happy to draft the route-map and a sample BGP config you can drop into your change ticket.

Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
